newsitem.title: CHINA: At least 32 killed in China airliner crash - papers.
newsitem.headline: At least 32 killed in China airliner crash - papers.

text.p: At least 32 people were killed and 29 seriously injured when a China Southern Airlines Boeing 737 crash-landed during a thunderstorm in the southern city of Shenzhen, Hong Kong newspapers said on Friday.
Officials in the booming city declined to confirm the death toll, but said at least 10 people were killed when the airliner crashed and burned.
The cause of the crash -- the first major civil aviation disaster reported in China for almost three years -- was unclear.
Flight CZ3456 had 74 people on board when it crashed at around 9.30 p.m. (1330 GMT) on Thursday at Shenzhen's Huangtian airport, killing at least 32 people, the South China Morning Post said.
The flight had originally been scheduled to land at Shenzhen's international airport but had been diverted to the new Huangtian airport because of heavy rain.
It was not immediately known if foreigners were among the dead. Staff at one Shenzhen hospital said two middle-aged Thai men had been injured but that their condition was not serious.
